sections.h2: Where Guadalupe County deed and lien records are kept
sections.html:
The County Clerk's Official Records Division in Seguin records deeds, mortgages, liens, plats and federal and state tax liens for Guadalupe County. The clerk is also the county recorder under the Texas Constitution, so a deed for any house in the county lands here regardless of where the owner lives. The county sits roughly one hundred miles inland from the Gulf of Mexico in south central Texas, part of the San Antonio metropolitan area.

Walk-in filers go to 211 West Court Street, Seguin, Texas 78155. A satellite office is at 1101 Elbel, Schertz, Texas 78154. Clerk staff cannot give legal advice or help draft wills, contracts or other legal instruments (Texas Government Code section 81.101), so have a deed prepared before you arrive. Call the Official Records Division before a trip to ask about hours and which services each counter offers.

The clerk's online Public Records Search lets anyone look up documents recorded under a name. Search your own name before listing the home to see each deed, lien and release attached to it, and show anything unfamiliar to a title company early.

Deeds can be hand-delivered, mailed or submitted through an e-recording vendor. The clerk uses CSC, eRecording Partners Network (ePN), Simplifile, HopDox and ValueCheck for electronic filings.

The county sets its own formatting rules, and they are strict. Leave at least four inches at the foot of the document for the recording stamp. If the page does not have the space, an add-a-page goes on at no charge, and e-recording submitters can attach the clerk's Submitters Add-A-Page as the last sheet. Scans must be 600 dpi with a white background, black lettering and a font of at least 8 points, because the image becomes the permanent record.

  • To be recorded, a conveyance must be signed and then acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer, or proved by two subscribing witnesses.
  • Deeds signed after December 31, 1981 need a mailing address for every grantee. Leave it out and the filer owes a penalty of $25 or double the recording fee, whichever is larger.
  • A properly prepared document must be recorded. The clerk has no power to turn one away because it might be fraudulent.

Base recording charges come from state law, as summarized in the county clerk manual that Texas courts publish for clerks. Page count, indexed names and added fees all change the total, so ask the clerk for the exact figure before mailing payment.

Recording fee building blocks from the Texas county clerk manual
ChargeAmount
First page$5.00
Each additional page or attachment$4.00
Each name over five indexed$0.25
Records management and preservation feeNot more than $10
Records archive feeNot more than $10
Records technology and infrastructure fee$2.00

A commissioners court may order its clerk not to charge recording fees on real property for buyers in particular federal or state grant programs. If your buyer uses one, ask whether Guadalupe County has done so.

sections.h2: Getting a Guadalupe County deed ready to file
sections.html:
Before you head to Seguin or Schertz, check five things. The deed carries every signature, and the notary has completed the acknowledgment. Each grantee's mailing address is printed on it. There is at least four inches of blank space at the foot of the last page. The legal description matches the prior deed. You have a check or payment ready, since the exact total depends on pages and names.

If anything is wrong, the clerk cannot fix or draft it for you, so ask a title company or attorney. For a house with a mortgage, ask who files the release of lien after payoff. A cash buyer's closing usually adds just the deed and any lien releases to the clerk's queue.

Register for the clerk's free Recording Notification Service and an email arrives whenever a document is recorded under a name you watch. One registered email address can watch up to 10 names or variations, and the alert covers only Guadalupe County records filed after you sign up.

Scammers record fake deeds to pose as owners, then collect rent or sale money from victims. A recorded document stays permanent, and the only remedy is a court order, itself recorded, declaring it void. The clerk cannot take legal action for you. Owners who suspect fraud should contact the Guadalupe County Sheriff's Office at 830-303-4188 extension 1219, an attorney, the Federal Trade Commission at reportfraud.ftc.gov or the Texas Attorney General's consumer complaint page.

Vacant houses are the usual target. Check on empty property often, ask someone you trust to look in while you are away, let no mail pile up, and keep your mailing address current with the Guadalupe Appraisal District and the tax assessor-collector.

sections.h2: Records that come up when a house changes hands
sections.html:
A title search follows the chain of recorded instruments. Deeds of trust, releases, tax liens, foreclosure notices, probate orders and affidavits all end up in the clerk's files, and a missing link slows a closing.

  • Foreclosure auctions are preceded by a notice on the courthouse door and in the clerk's file, at least 21 days out.
  • The comptroller files notice of a state tax lien with the clerk, who enters it in the state tax lien book.
  • When a will is probated as a muniment of title, the order and will go to the clerk of the county where the land is.
  • A small estate affidavit that passes a homestead gets a recorded copy at the clerk's office.
  • A transfer on death deed has no effect unless it was recorded while the owner was alive.

Heirs sometimes discover that an old deed was never recorded. An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement on file, but no buyer or lender has to rely on it. When title is unclear, a court order holds up better.

sections.h2: Guadalupe County housing at a glance
sections.html:
The July 2025 estimate is 201,111 residents, a gain of 16.4 percent over the 172,729 on the April 2020 base. They share 77,249 housing units across 711.25 square miles, and the county issued 1,697 building permits in 2025, so new deeds and plats keep arriving at the clerk's counter. Homeowners occupy 77.8 percent of homes. The 2020 to 2024 middle home value is $304,400, and the middle rent is $1,517.

For tax questions the Guadalupe Appraisal District's number is 830.303.3313. The district values property at its January 1 status. It also describes deferrals that postpone tax without canceling it: a homestead deferral accrues 8 percent a year, and a deferral for owners 65 or older or disabled accrues 5 percent. Settle any deferral before closing on a sale.

faqs.q: Who records a deed for Guadalupe County land?
faqs.a: The County Clerk's Official Records Division at 211 West Court Street, Seguin, Texas 78155, or the Schertz satellite office at 1101 Elbel. Electronic filers go through CSC, ePN, Simplifile, HopDox or ValueCheck.

faqs.q: Does a document need a notary to be recorded?
faqs.a: In practice, yes. A conveyance needs a notary's or other authorized officer's acknowledgment, or proof before two subscribing witnesses. The clerk records qualifying documents in the order received.

faqs.q: How do I learn if a document was recorded against my property?
faqs.a: Look yourself up in the clerk's online records, then join the free Recording Notification Service. Each registered address can watch up to 10 names and gets an automated message on any new filing.

faqs.q: Can a fraudulent deed be removed?
faqs.a: No. A recorded document stays permanent, and only a court order recorded afterward shows that it is void. Contact the Sheriff's Office and an attorney quickly if you suspect fraud.

faqs.q: What does recording a deed cost?
faqs.a: Page one is $5.00 under state rules, each added page is $4.00, and each name past five is $0.25. Management, archive and technology fees go on top, so ask the clerk to quote the total.
